# PART 2 – The claim, its estimand and its causal graph {#part-2-the-claim-its-estimand-and-its-causal-graph .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Part 2 · 90 minutes
:::

::: notes
Part two. The case of the day is a study in demography, about the first time that American women lived with a partner before any marriage, and how often those couples went on to marry. It compares unions begun in the early 1990s with unions begun in the late 2000s, using two waves of a large national survey. Five analysts in Multi100 reanalysed one of its claims, all five from the same file, and they reached three different conclusions. This part does not explain that split yet; it keeps it in view. We go inside the paper first, then step back to two studies that show how often disagreement among analysts is disagreement about the question. Then we build the estimand and the causal graph, and use both on a feature of this claim that is easy to miss: everyone in the data cohabited, and who cohabits changed.
:::
